instructions:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up.
3. Walk both hands about 20 cm to one side to rotate your body around, then perform another push-up.
4. Keep walking your hands in the same direction to complete the full circle, doing a push-up at each position.
5. Brace your core so your hips stay level throughout.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips from sagging by squeezing your glutes and bracing your abs.
2. Move your hands with control to protect your wrists and shoulders.
3. Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
4. Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to your torso, not flared out.

instructions:
1. Lie flat on the bench with feet planted on the floor and eyes under the barbell.
2. Grip the bar with hands slightly closer than shoulder-width, palms facing away.
3. Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with straight arms.
4. Lower the bar to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
5. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
2. Tuck your elbows close to your sides to load the triceps.
3. Lower the bar under control to your lower sternum.
4. Exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Start in a plank with hands close together under your chest and arms straight.
2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
4. Press through your palms to push back up to straight arms.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs to load the triceps.
2. Lower under control to maximize muscle engagement.
3. Brace your core so your hips do not sag.
4. Exhale as you push up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Grip the bar with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
2. Hang with arms fully extended and legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
3. Pull your body up by driving your elbows down and contracting your biceps until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower yourself under control until your arms are fully extended.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive your elbows down and pull your chest to the bar.
2. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
3. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell on the floor, gripping it overhand just wider than shoulder-width.
2. Pull the bar from the floor, then explosively extend your hips and knees and shrug to drive it upward.
3. Drop under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders while squatting until your thighs pass below your knees.
4. Drive up out of the squat and continue pressing the bar overhead until your arms are straight.
5. Lower the bar back to your shoulders, then to the floor under control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep the bar close to your body during the pull.
2. Catch the bar with elbows high and your torso upright.
3. Use leg drive to start the overhead press, not just your arms.
4. Brace your core throughout to protect your lower back.
